Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a fundamental error in biological fact-checking by incorrectly asserting that "cell wall" is common to both plant and animal cells. While the Planner attempted to justify this by equating the animal extracellular matrix/glycocalyx with a cell wall, this is a scientifically invalid equivalence in the context of standard cell biology questions. Animal cells do not possess a cell wall; the cell wall is a rigid structure found only in plants, fungi, and bacteria. Consequently, the Planner selected option C (which includes cell wall) as the correct answer, ignoring the fact that option B (cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondrion) contains structures that are universally present in both cell types (with the caveat of mature red blood cells being a specific exception often ignored in general multiple-choice contexts compared to the absolute absence of cell walls in animals). The error stems from a misinterpretation of the question's scope and a failure to verify basic biological definitions before concluding.
